You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Broadcom Q3 Preview: Growth Is Priced In, Conversion Is What Matters — JPMorgan Says AI Is Badly Underestimated and Google TPU Fears Are Overdone

TEXT:
1. Investment Snapshot
Broadcom ( AVGO .US) will report fiscal third-quarter 2026 results after the U.S. close on September 2, 2026 . Management has guided quarterly revenue to about $29.4 billion ( +84% YoY ), including AI semiconductor revenue of about $16 billion ( over +200% YoY ). Street consensus is roughly $29.2–$29.5 billion in revenue and adjusted EPS of about $3.22 ( +90.5% YoY ). Ahead of the print, JPMorgan kept an Overweight rating and a $580 price target , arguing the quarter should come in solid and that Q4 guidance is more likely to set the stock. Shares have pulled back meaningfully from the highs, options imply about an 8% move, and the debate has shifted from “is it growing?” to whether order conversion, customer mix, and margins can hold at the same time.
2. Four Things That Matter
Focus 1: Can the $16 billion AI semiconductor guide be delivered?
Q2 AI semiconductor revenue already reached $10.8 billion ( +143% YoY ), with bookings of more than $30 billion —well ahead of shipments. The Q3 guide requires another step-up. The test is whether custom accelerators (XPU/TPU) and AI networking ramps together. A print at or above $16 billion would reinforce the “second-half acceleration” story. A clear miss would reopen questions on capacity, customer timing, or revenue recognition.
Focus 2: Q4 guidance and the path to $56 billion of full-year AI revenue
Q3 consensus already sits near the company midpoint, so the after-hours reaction is more likely to hinge on the Q4 outlook. Street Q4 revenue is around $34.9 billion . Management has pointed to full-year AI semiconductor revenue of about $56 billion ( about +180% YoY ) and reiterated fiscal 2027 AI revenue of more than $100 billion . An upward Q4 revision, or a clearer gigawatt delivery cadence, is what the market needs to digest elevated expectations. An in-line guide may be read as visibility peaking.
Focus 3: Google TPU share versus customer diversification
Google remains the largest customer, and the stock keeps trading rumors of in-house / MediaTek share shift. Street base case is that Broadcom’s multi-generation TPU work with Google is still the plan of record, while Anthropic , OpenAI , Meta and others support a fiscal 2027 shipment outlook of about 10 GW . The tell is not another design-win headline. It is funded capacity, site readiness, and purchase-order conversion. Lower customer concentration is what would move the valuation from a “single-customer premium” to a “platform premium.”
Focus 4: Mix-driven margins and cash flow
A higher AI hardware mix pressures gross margin. The company expects Q3 non-GAAP operating margin of about 67% and adjusted EBITDA of about 68% of revenue, with gross margin likely easing from about 77% in Q2 to about 74% . Q2 free cash flow was about $10.26 billion , or about 46% of revenue; software remains the profit and cash-flow ballast. If margins fall faster than guided and software growth does not offset it, the market may re-label “high growth” as “lower quality.”
3. Upside and Downside
Upside catalysts:
AI semiconductor revenue at or above $16 billion , with networking holding its share—confirmation of a compute-plus-interconnect flywheel.
Q4 revenue guidance clearly above the roughly $34.9 billion consensus, plus more specific 2027 delivery and order-conversion detail.
Management addresses Google share concerns and shows other top-tier customers ramping, easing the concentration narrative.
Downside risks:
Results only meet the midpoint and Q4 commentary is cautious, inviting profit-taking after a high-expectation setup.
Gross margin or operating margin slips below the roughly 67%–68% band, raising fears that a rising ASIC mix is eroding earnings quality.
Large-customer timing noise, competitors entering custom silicon, or financing/leverage headlines weighing on risk appetite.
4. Trading Framework
Bull case: AI revenue is delivered with a constructive Q4 outlook, customer mix improves, and margins stay on guide. That combination could support a valuation repair from the pullback. The long beat streak still makes “beat and raise” the strongest setup.
Bear case: Numbers are merely in line, margins compress more than expected, or management ducks share and conversion detail. That can trigger the two-way move already priced in options, especially if high growth is already in the stock.
Key numbers:
Total revenue and YoY growth
Whether AI semiconductor revenue reaches about $16 billion
Q4 revenue and margin guidance
Gross margin, operating margin, and free cash flow
Tactical notes:
Into the print: Price is hugging the 200-day moving average; risk/reward is only average. Keep event risk light. Avoid adding leveraged longs below 368 .
Long setup: A close back above 379–385 , with pullbacks holding 368 . Upside references 391 / 400 . Stops can sit at 365 , or below 350 depending on risk tolerance.
Short / hedge setup: A gap that cannot reclaim 368 , or a failed push through 377–385 . Downside references 356 / 350 / 340 .
